faq.a: A shift is a set block of work time. A night shift runs through the night, for example from 9 pm to 7 am, so important work never stops.
asks: Why do some people work at night?

faq.q: Why do nurses work at night?
faq.a: People in hospital still need care at night: medicine, checks and comfort. So nurses and doctors take turns, with some working nights while others sleep.
asks: Tell me about nurses on duty

faq.q: Who answers emergency calls at night?
faq.a: Trained call takers work in shifts all day and night. They ask what is wrong and send fire engines, ambulances or police. The number differs by country, such as 112 in Europe and India, 911 in the USA and 999 in the UK.
asks: What number do I call in an emergency?

faq.q: Why do bakers start so early?
faq.a: Bread takes hours to mix, rise and bake. To have fresh loaves ready when shops open in the morning, many bakers start work at around 2 to 4 am.
asks: What time do bakers get up?

faq.q: How do night helpers make my morning possible?
faq.a: While you sleep, people keep power on, answer emergencies, bake bread and clean streets. So when you wake up, everything you need is ready.
asks: Tell me about you wake up
Who helps me while I sleep?

facts: 112 works as an emergency number across the European Union and on most mobile phones worldwide; India adopted 112 as its single emergency number.
Many countries have rules limiting night work for young people under 18 to protect their health.
